and a GET it needs refuses, so the page renders empty. The gate
`screen-route-permission-fit.py --check` fails on any triple absent from this list AND on any
triple here that no longer occurs, so the list can be neither a ceiling nor a graveyard.

become fourteen different mismatches and the gate would stay quiet.

declared.decision: ITEM 5 — ALREADY BUILT, and this row is a blind spot of the measurement rather than a defect. Verified by reading the screen: the role fieldset sits inside `{canIssueLogin ? ...}`, where `canIssueLogin` is `hasPermission(user, 'user.manage')` — and BRANCH_DEPARTMENT_MANAGER does not hold that code. So the field is already hidden, and the loader's effect early-returns on the same flag, which means `GET /rbac/roles` is never called for this role at all. The else branch already names the reason bilingually: `reducedCapability(t, 'empLoginCanAct', 'empLoginCannotAct', 'user.manage')`, beside a comment saying exactly why — "an absent control with no explanation reads as a missing feature". THE BLIND SPOT, STATED RATHER THAN CLOSED: this check maps a screen's IMPORTS to routes and cannot see that a call sits behind a screen-computed permission flag. Teaching it that was considered and NOT done, because the obvious rule — treat any call inside a try/catch as handled — would have hidden the original `/provider-register-office` defect, which was also inside a try/catch and was real. The row therefore stays declared with this reading recorded, rather than the measurement being loosened until the row disappears.
